item.title: Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Smuggling, power, profit: Irregular migration out of eastern Libya
item.description: There is currently more irregular migration between eastern Libya and Crete, Greece. It's raising questions as to what connects people smugglers with powerful militias in eastern Libya and then in turn, Europeans.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
item.description: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Seoul fears being sidelined as US reaches out to North Korea
item.description: With ties between South Korea and the Trump administration strained, the South Korean government worries that Donald Trump's pursuit of a diplomatic breakthrough with Kim Jong Un may come at Seoul's expense.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Bollywood and the underworld — together in the spotlight?
item.description: A wave of shootings and extortion threats has rattled India's film industry. This time, those claiming responsibility are very different from the Mumbai underworld that had Bollywood in its grip back in the 1990s.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
item.description: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.
item.dc:subject: Germany

item.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
item.description: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: China leaders demand more loyalty and more initiative
item.description: The CCP session emphasized internal discipline, as expected, but left the question of Xi Jinping's successor unanswered. The party seems anxious of any instability as geopolitics heats up and China's economy cools down.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Human trafficking victims stranded in Guinea-Bissau
item.description: Dozens of West Africans lured to Guinea-Bissau with promises of jobs and migration to Europe say they were exploited by a suspected trafficking network. Now many cannot afford to return home.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Can EU and India work together to secure Indo-Pacific?
item.description: India and Europe are deepening defense ties, but their clashing perspectives on Russia and differing priorities on China are hampering their joint ambitions on maritime security.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.
